gary_2026_09_21_building_for_the_future_.title: Building For The Future - Data Centers, Water Stewardship & Decarbonization
gary_2026_09_21_building_for_the_future_.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_21_building_for_the_future_.summary: Gary's Guide: Two of the hardest problems in corporate climate action right now are water & energy, & both are being tested in real time by companies making infrastructure decisions with long lifespans. This event brings together cross-sector practitioners to discuss what's working, what's stuck, & what needs to change to achieve meaningful, shared solutions at scale. Panel one - data centers & water: Water is an increasing source of tension as data center development accelerates. Data center developers are setting water positive commitments that include reducing water demand & increasing reuse, & also investing in water replenishment that goes beyond the fenceline to invest in watersheds. In this panel, we will bring together speakers representing hyperscalers, utilities, & communities to explore what is needed to effectively support communities & ecosystems while reducing data center risks. Panel two - portfolio decarbonization: Setting a corporate emissions target is straightforward; delivering it across a portfolio of facilities built over decades is not. Public & private sector panelists will discuss how large organizations sequence capital across sites with different ages, uses, & local grids - where electrification pencils out, where it doesn't yet, & what actually moves a portfolio rather than a single flagship building.

gary_2026_09_21_when_data_goes_dark_prep.title: When Data Goes Dark - Preparing For Climate Disasters In Era Of Science Disinvestment
gary_2026_09_21_when_data_goes_dark_prep.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_21_when_data_goes_dark_prep.summary: Gary's Guide: Over the past year, climate science & environmental data & tools have faced steep disinvestment, but maintaining a strong scientific enterprise & the data it creates is critical to helping communities & businesses prepare for & respond to climate risks. When that data disappears, so does our ability to anticipate, prepare for, & respond to climate disasters before they strike. This panel starts by looking at what's been lost, & at the rescue efforts now underway to preserve high-fidelity climate data & disaster-cost datasets before they disappear for good. It then turns forward: what will it take to rebuild a more resilient, connected environmental data ecosystem - one built so that this kind of loss can't happen again? Join us for a conversation that moves from triage to reimagining, bringing together leaders in climate science, environmental data, global research, & emergency management to chart what comes next. Sponsored By: American Geophysical Union Climate Central The New York Climate Exchange Open Environmental Data Project

gary_2026_09_22_how_data_center_fights_r.title: How Data Center Fights Renewing Local Power Across US
gary_2026_09_22_how_data_center_fights_r.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_22_how_data_center_fights_r.summary: Gary's Guide: This is an in-person event happening as part of NYC Climate Week. To hear many in the tech industry tell it, data centers will bring wealth & prosperity not only to those who build them, but to the communities that ultimately live with & around them. However, drawing a longer historical arc is essential: AI is proposed as a new industrial moonshot in communities that have already seen the rise & fall of steel factories, coal plants, fracking infrastructure, & more. Today's companies are trying to sell communities on yet another industrial vision. On Sept. 22 at 5:30 p.m., join us in Midtown East, Manhattan, for a panel discussion featuring journalists, nonprofits, & community organizers who are uncovering the impact of data centers across the country & sharing that information with the public. Our panel discussion will feature Maia Woluchem, program director of Data & Society's Trustworthy Infrastructures program; Alejandra Martinez, The Texas Tribune environmental reporter & Pulitzer Center grantee; Brian Crawford, Texas resident with the nonprofit Protect the Paluxy Valley; & Ginny Marcille-Kerslake, Pennsylvania resident & Senior Organizer at Food & Water Watch. Kit R. Roane, award-winning senior producer at Retro Report, will be the moderator. This event is anchored by the launch of Data & Society's forthcoming report, The AI Factory: Data Centers, Power & Resistance in Late Industrial Pennsylvania, a landmark study emerging out of eighteen months of field research in the Keystone State, as well as Pulitzer Center-supported reporting on data center development by The Texas Tribune. Light refreshments will be served. Seating is limited, & R.S.V.P. is required. This panel discussion is co-organized by Data & Society, Retro Report, & The Pulitzer Center.

gary_2026_09_22_tech_x_market_decoders.summary: Gary's Guide: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 6 pm - check-in. We kick off at 6.15 pm. 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Drone delivery gets regulatory approval - Now what? DoorDash just became only the eighth company ever to earn FAA air-carrier certification for drones, joining Amazon, Walmart, & Alphabet's Wing in a race that's now more about economics than regulation. We're decoding whether drone delivery can actually scale profitably or whether the real bottleneck was never the FAA to begin with. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.label: Music / Movies
jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.place: ART HOUSE, 345 MARIN BLVD, JERSEY CITY
jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.summary: Experience the groundbreaking Tony Award-winning musical and Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that defined a generation. Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City’s East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them. Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship. This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions’ 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.

jc_culture_43488_2026_09_25_jersey_city_.summary: The Jersey City Poetry Festival (JCPOFEST) is an interdisciplinary, intergenerational event taking place September 25–27 under this year’s theme “Viva! jc_culture_10004823_2026_09_25_the_socie.title: The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) 91st Annual Members Exhibition 2026
jc_culture_10004823_2026_09_25_the_socie.label: Art / Culture
jc_culture_10004823_2026_09_25_the_socie.place: MANA CONTEMPORARY, 888 NEWARK AVE., JERSEY CITY
jc_culture_10004823_2026_09_25_the_socie.summary: 91st Annual Members Exhibition The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) is excited to announce its upcoming 91st Annual Members Exhibition, to be held at Mana Contemporary in Jersey City from September 11–27, 2026 (Fridays and Saturdays, 3:00–7:00 PM; Sundays, 12:00–3:00 PM). The exhibition will feature 200 hand-pulled prints representing a broad range of printmaking techniques and subjects, created by SAGA artists from across the country. Awards will be juried by Leslie Diuguid, founder of Du-Good Press in Brooklyn. The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) is a nonprofit organization established in 1915 whose mission is to promote contemporary printmakers, cultivate printmaking appreciation and education, and provide a collaborative and inclusive platform for artists across the country. https://sagaprints.com/ Hosting this year’s exhibition is Monira Foundation, an independent nonprofit institution that functions as a radical experimental laboratory, working in close collaboration with artists, curators, musicians, dancers, producers, and writers to conceive, realize, and present innovative projects in all media. Monira is located within Mana Contemporary, a 2-million-square-foot art center. The complex occupies a renovated 100-year-old former tobacco warehouse, featuring expansive exhibition spaces, working artist studios, the International Center of Photography archives, and more. A free public reception and awards ceremony with participating artists will be held on Saturday, September 26, from 3:00–5:00 PM. Guests are invited to enjoy light refreshments while celebrating the diversity and innovation of contemporary printmaking. WHEN Exhibition: Fridays–Sundays, September 11–27, 2026 Public Reception & Awards Ceremony: Saturday, September 26, 2026 3:00–5:00 PM WHERE Mana Contemporary 888 Newark Avenue Jersey City, NJ 07306
